output_json.patch_notes:
Shell.java: added a configurable `executableEscapePattern` field (mirroring the existing `argumentEscapePattern`, default \"\\%s\" preserving prior behavior for the base Shell class and CmdShell), and changed the executable-quoting call in getRawCommandLine() to use it instead of a hardcoded plain-backslash escape char.

BourneShell.java: changed the executable quote delimiter from '\"' to '\'' and enabled single-quote escaping for the executable (setSingleQuotedExecutableEscaped(true), setExecutableEscapePattern(\"'\\%s'\")) — identical settings to what already safely protects arguments. Added '\"' to BASH_QUOTING_TRIGGER_CHARS so executables containing a bare literal double-quote are still safely wrapped. Removed the getExecutable() override that pre-quoted via unifyQuotes()/double-quotes (now redundant and unsafe given the new single-quote sink); the inherited raw getter is used instead, and Shell#getRawCommandLine() performs all quoting/escaping once, safely. getExecutionPreamble()'s working-directory quoting (still via unifyQuotes) was intentionally left unchanged — it's outside the alert's traced executable/argument sink and has its own exact-string-matching tests.

Added regression tests: BourneShellTest gains 5 new cases asserting the generated shell command line for executables containing $(...), backticks, ';', embedded single quotes (verifying correct '\\''-escaping), and confirming plain executables remain unquoted. CommandlineTest gains an end-to-end functional test that actually executes Commandline with executable \"true$(touch <marker>)\" and asserts the marker file is never created (i.e., the injected command never runs), skipped on Windows since BourneShell is POSIX-shell-specific.
output_json.risk_notes: Behavior change is scoped to BourneShell's executable quoting only: executables with no shell-special characters (the common case, e.g. \"chmod\", \"/usr/bin/echo\") remain unquoted exactly as before (verified). Executables containing metacharacters or quote characters now render as a single-quoted, escaped token instead of an unsafe double-quoted one — functionally equivalent for legitimate paths (e.g. paths with embedded quote characters used in the existing quotedpath/apostrophe tests still resolve to the correct literal filename and were verified to execute correctly), but any code that scrapes/parses the exact string form of Commandline#getExecutable() or the shell command line for a BourneShell executable containing special characters will see single quotes instead of double quotes. No test in the existing suite (289 tests, all passing) or in this codebase relies on that exact format. CmdShell (Windows) and the intentional isQuotedArgumentsEnabled(false) raw-argument opt-out were left unchanged — the former can't be exercised/verified on this Linux build and redesigning cmd.exe quoting carries real regression risk without Windows CI; the latter is a documented caller-opt-in escape hatch, not a default-path vulnerability. Full mvn test (289 tests) and the provided POV (before: VULNERABLE/exit 0 marker created; after: NOT VULNERABLE/exit 1, no marker) were both verified in the project's Docker container.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-078 OS command injection in org.codehaus.plexus.util.cli.Commandline/Shell/BourneShell. The root cause was that BourneShell.getExecutable() quoted the executable string with double quotes (via unifyQuotes()/StringUtils.quoteAndEscape) without escaping POSIX shell metacharacters ($(...), backticks, ;, |, &, etc.), while double quotes in /bin/sh do not suppress command substitution. Since BourneShell is the default shell on Linux/macOS, any caller of Commandline#setExecutable(String) with a not-fully-trusted string could inject and execute arbitrary shell commands via Runtime.exec(). Arguments were already safely single-quoted by BourneShell; the fix extends that same proven-safe single-quote-wrap-with-escape mechanism to the executable, and removes the redundant/unsafe double-quote pre-processing (unifyQuotes) for the executable path, while leaving working-directory quoting, CmdShell (Windows), and the intentional unquoted-argument opt-out untouched (out of the alert's confirmed/traced scope and not exercisable/verifiable on this Linux build).
